safety_checks.detail: A second writer cannot commit using an earlier revision; journal unchanged.
Current write revision cannot launder an older reasoning receipt.
Even a preferred requirement must be acknowledged; unmet preference alone need not block PASS.
The word met cannot silently satisfy an exception predicate.
An unknown hard requirement keeps PASS unavailable.
A fabricated quote cannot become checked document evidence.
Both source versions retain byte hashes; retrieval ignores later edits to the original file.
Hash verification detects modified retained bytes before state use.
A new source invalidates direct and derived facts, decisions and prior task completion.
Retiring a cited fact also invalidates copied downstream facts, even when not labelled derived.
Exact raw steering must be reconciled before a new dispatch.
A pause survives capture/reconciliation and still prevents workflow dispatch.
An earlier physical response cannot complete against newer user requirements.
Reconciled user text does not settle the old physical call or its usage.
Unknown token usage pauses new spending.
A measured ceiling overrun remains recorded and prevents another call.
Stable budget IDs cannot change economic scope or unit.
A caller cannot bypass an unknown task-bound budget with an empty dispatch list.
Same dispatch usage is counted once; conflicting telemetry is rejected.
A paused parent goal also pauses its prerequisite work, not just its own dispatch.
A saved source document cannot bypass an unfinished prerequisite task.
An unresolved material question prevents a current decision receipt for affected work.
Insufficient context capacity is an explicit failure, not omitted requirements.
Fresh recovery exposes pending input that arrived after the saved checkpoint.
